title: Tomographic Reconstruction of Infrared Radiance from Axisymmetric Sprays in a Hot Environment Using Multi-Parameter Regularization
abstract: This study proposes a robust algorithm for tomographic reconstruction of infrared radiance from an axisymmetric fuel spray in a hot environment by directly solving the radiative transfer equation. The proposed algorithm combines differential infrared thermography (DIT) with multi-parameter regularized inversion. First, the DIT emissivity is used to reconstruct the local extinction coefficient, and the local radiative source term is then recovered by solving the attenuated line-of-sight integral. To stabilize the ill-posed inversion, a global smoothness penalty is combined with an additional center-axis constraint that imposes the zero-gradient condition required by axisymmetry. A numerical phantom study, including configurations relevant to evaporating cold sprays and flashing jets, is conducted to evaluate the reconstruction accuracy under well-defined conditions and noisy measurement scenarios.The results demonstrate that the proposed method extends conventional DIT beyond the equivalent-slab approximation by resolving the line-of-sight-integrated emissivity into a local extinction field and accounting for self-attenuation within the spatially resolved axisymmetric spray structure. This approach allows reconstruction of the local radiative source term and local radiance with good agreement with the ground truth in the main spray region. Consequently, this establishes an IR-tomographic framework for recovering the internal radiance and potentially the temperature field of axisymmetric sprays with appropriate radiometric calibration.An additional noise-suppression strategy is introduced to improve reconstruction robustness at higher noise levels.
